detailed_rationale: Torrent Power is a diversified, largely-regulated power utility: licensed distribution in Ahmedabad/Surat/Dahej-SEZ/Dholera-SIR/DNH/Daman plus franchised distribution in Agra and Bhiwandi-Shil-Mumbra-Kalwa (~4.2 million customers), 2,730MW gas-based + 362MW coal-based thermal generation, and a renewable book (~1,081MWp solar + 921MW wind operational, with a targeted 10GW RE portfolio by 2030 and ~4.3GW currently under installation). [DATA] FY26 (year ended Mar-2026) consolidated revenue was ~Rs 28,966cr, roughly flat YoY, while consolidated PAT fell to ~Rs 2,469cr (down ~19% YoY from ~Rs 3,053cr in FY25; FY26 EPS Rs 47.95 vs Rs 61.23 in FY25) [source: SolarQuarter/ScanX FY26 press coverage]. Q4FY26 standalone-quarter PAT fell ~70% YoY to Rs 318cr on revenue of Rs 6,406cr (down only ~0.8% YoY) [source: Business Standard, Univest]. This is NOT primarily an operating collapse: FY25's base was inflated by a one-time non-cash deferred-tax-liability reversal of ~Rs 637cr that does not repeat in FY26, and Q4FY26 additionally carried a regulatory disallowance of ~Rs 171cr tied to Uno Sujan power-purchase-cost capping for FY24-25 that management flagged as likely recoverable (a similar Rs 273cr item was previously allowed by the regulator) [source: Torrent Power Q4FY26 earnings call transcript / Yahoo Finance summary]. Net of these, the underlying quarter is closer to flat-to-modestly-down, still pressured by gas-based generation margins in a soft/volatile merchant power and gas-price environment. The quant model's own scores corroborate a currently-weak growth print rather than distress: growth_1y_score is very low (11.0/100) and growth_3y_score modest (22.5/100), consistent with the reported ~4% 3yr revenue CAGR and roughly flat trailing-12m growth [DATA, from resultsull750_scored.csv row], while quality_score is high (85.7/100) and both bs_flag and liquidity_flag are GREEN (D/E 0.73x, interest coverage ~6.0x) [DATA]. On the growth-capex side, the company is mid-cycle on a large capacity build: renewable capex of ~Rs 6,010cr in FY26 with a step-up guided for FY27, 1.2-1.5GW/year commissioning pace, plus a >Rs 30,000cr thermal expansion program comprising a new 1,600MW Madhya Pradesh plant under construction and the acquired 1,400MW Nabha Power asset consolidating into the group from Q1FY27 [source: SaurEnergy, PowerPeakDigest, Q4FY26 concall]. Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026) results have not yet been reported as of this review (board meeting date not yet announced in searches run 2026-07-21); some analyst previews flag a further ~50% YoY PAT decline expectation for the quarter given a strong Q1FY26 comparison base, which is a base-effect call-out, not new information about the franchise's health.
recommendation_rationale: The quant model's overall call is Sell, driven almost entirely by the 1-year composite (final_score_1y 33.8, Sell zone) dragging down an otherwise Hold-zone 3-year score (final_score_3y 48.9) -- the 1y weakness traces to trailing revenue/profit growth that is substantially a base-effect and one-off-driven distortion (FY25 DTA reversal, Q4FY26 regulatory disallowance) rather than a genuine deterioration in the regulated distribution franchise or the thermal/renewable asset base. Balance sheet is GREEN, quality_score is high, and the company sits mid-way through a credible, already-financed multi-year capacity-doubling program (RE to 10GW by 2030, Nabha + new MP thermal) that the trailing-12m screen cannot see. That combination -- healthy balance sheet, high quality score, an explainable trailing-growth dip, and a funded forward capacity pipeline -- is a defensible basis to rescue Sell to Hold rather than confirm the quant Sell. It stops short of a Buy-equivalent conviction because the valuation (29.6x trailing PE, on an already-depressed earnings base once one-offs are stripped) leaves little room for execution slippage on the Nabha integration or thermal commissioning timeline, and gas-generation margin pressure is a genuine, ongoing headwind, not a one-off.
summary: Torrent Power's headline profit numbers look weak this year (FY26 PAT down ~19%, Q4 down ~70%), but a large part of that is a high FY25 comparison base (a one-time tax-reversal gain) and a regulatory cost item under dispute that the company expects to recover -- not a breakdown in the underlying distribution-and-generation business, which remains a stable, largely-regulated franchise (Ahmedabad/Surat licensed distribution plus Agra/Bhiwandi franchises) with a healthy balance sheet. The company is also mid-way through a large, funded capacity build (renewables toward 10GW by 2030, plus a new thermal plant and the Nabha Power acquisition) that should support growth over the next few years even though it doesn't show up in this year's numbers yet. We keep it on Hold: the business quality and balance sheet support staying invested, but the current valuation already prices in a fair amount of that future growth, leaving limited margin for delays in the capacity build-out.
positive_para: A predominantly regulated/quasi-regulated earnings base (licensed distribution in Ahmedabad/Surat plus long-standing franchise areas) gives Torrent Power more revenue stability than a pure merchant power name, and the balance sheet is genuinely clean (D/E 0.73x, interest coverage ~6x, GREEN bs/liquidity flags) with a high quant quality_score (85.7/100). The FY26/Q4FY26 profit decline is largely explained by non-recurring items -- the FY25 one-time deferred-tax reversal (~Rs 637cr) not repeating, and a Q4FY26 regulatory power-purchase-cost disallowance (~Rs 171cr) management expects to eventually recover -- rather than a structural earnings problem. Meanwhile the company has a funded, multi-year capacity-expansion program in motion: renewables toward a 10GW-by-2030 target (~4.3GW currently under installation, 1.2-1.5GW/year commissioning pace) and a >Rs 30,000cr thermal build-out (new 1,600MW MP plant plus the 1,400MW Nabha Power acquisition consolidating from Q1FY27), which gives a visible path to capacity-led earnings growth over FY27-30 that the trailing-12-month screen cannot capture.
negative_para: Strip out the one-offs and the underlying growth is still unimpressive: 3yr revenue CAGR of only ~4% and roughly flat trailing-12m growth (quant growth_1y_score 11.0/100, growth_3y_score 22.5/100 -- both weak on a percentile basis), and gas-based generation continues to face margin pressure from volatile gas prices and soft merchant power demand, a genuine ongoing headwind rather than a one-off. At ~29.6x trailing PE the stock is not cheap for a utility, and that multiple sits on an earnings base already flattered by regulatory dispute assumptions (the Uno Sujan recovery is not yet confirmed) -- if the Nabha Power integration or the new thermal/renewable capacity slips its commissioning timeline, or gas-generation margins stay under pressure, the multiple has little cushion. The quant model's own sector_macro_1y_score is very weak (2.1/100), signaling a soft near-term power-sector macro read that could keep the trailing growth numbers depressed for another few quarters even before Q1FY27 (not yet reported as of 2026-07-21) is in hand.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~29.6x trailing consolidated PE (pe_for_ranking, [DATA]) the market is pricing meaningfully more growth than the trailing 3yr revenue CAGR (~4%) or the roughly-flat trailing-12m print would justify on their own -- but those trailing numbers are themselves depressed by one-off/base effects (FY25 DTA reversal, Q4FY26 regulatory disallowance), so the 'clean' run-rate multiple is somewhat lower than the headline 29.6x. The model's own cross-sectional value_score (58/100) treats the name as roughly mid-pack rather than extreme-rich, which is consistent with a fair-to-slightly-rich read: the multiple looks sustainable IF the company executes its already-financed capacity-doubling pipeline (RE to 10GW by 2030, Nabha 1,400MW + new 1,600MW MP thermal) broadly on the guided timeline, converting new capacity into regulated/contracted cash flows at a mid-teens RoE-type return; it looks rich if gas-generation margin pressure persists and/or the capacity build slips, in which case the stock is paying up for options that take longer to convert to earnings. ROE is 16.4% (below the 20% threshold that would trigger a dilution discussion under the exceptional-growth tier, and this call is not an exceptional-growth call in any case).
